about: Export presets for harness-video, by name: `harness-video SCENE.flecs OUT.mp4 PRESET`. The one home of every encoder setting; src/preset.rs reads it (compiled in) and refuses a field it does not know. A preset's width and height are pixels: the scene's Video says the frame in points, and the scale is the preset's width over the scene's (the two must have one aspect). `fps` replaces the scene's (a timeline is in seconds, so every frame is still drawn at its own time).

says: Recommended Video Codec: H264 High Profile

Video Resolution: 1280x720 (landscape), 720x1280 (portrait), 720x720 (square). Subscribed users can upload a 1080p video and get 1080p playback. Unsubscribed users can upload a 720p video and get a 720p playback.
Frame rate: must be 60 FPS or less
File size: see size and duration limits (8 GB default for Post video; 16 GB for Premium / verified)
Video on a Post (tweet_video, amplify_video): 0.5 seconds-20 minutes, 8 GB
Aspect ratio: must be between 1:3 and 3:1
Pixel format: Only YUV 4:2:0 is supported
Audio must be AAC with Low Complexity profile. (High-Efficiency AAC is not supported)
Audio must be mono or stereo, not 5.1 or greater
unverified: The page is the API's (media upload); the consumer help page help.x.com/en/using-x/x-videos answered 403 on 2026-11-11, so what the app and the web composer accept is not established.
HEVC / H.265 is not mentioned on the page: nothing says X accepts it.
10-bit and HDR are not mentioned: nothing says X keeps them. The X presets are 8-bit BT.709.
No container is named; MP4 with the moov first is what the presets write.

The page says both 'Dimensions: must be between 32x32 and 1280x1024' and 'Subscribed users can upload a 1080p video': 1920x1080 is taken to be for subscribed accounts only, and nothing above 1080p is accepted, so there is no 4K preset.
The Premium / verified duration limit (the page's second table) was not read out in full.

x-landscape-1080p60.for: X, a subscribed account (1080p in, 1080p playback): the page's recommended codec at its highest resolution and frame rate. X re-encodes whatever it is given, so the bitrate is far above its 5,000 kbps minimum: a clean source.

x-landscape-720p60.for: X, an unsubscribed account (720p in, 720p playback).

x-square-1080.for: X, 1:1, a subscribed account. For a scene whose Video says `reframes`.

x-portrait-1080x1920.for: X, 9:16, a subscribed account (most short video is watched upright). For a scene whose Video says `reframes`.

x-landscape-1080p60-hevc.for: UNVERIFIED ON X: its page names H.264 only. HEVC Main, 8-bit, for places that take it; never the default for X.

youtube-hdr10-master.for: YouTube's HDR master, and what a render with no preset named makes: H.265 Main 10, HDR10 (PQ over BT.2020, P3-D65 mastering display at 1000 nits), lossless audio. Its size and frame rate are the scene's own (0 here).
